title: Notre-Dame de Paris
blurb: The great French Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité in Paris, begun in 1163: twin 69 m west towers, three sculpted portals, the Gallery of Kings, flying buttresses, three rose windows, the great organ of nearly 8,000 pipes, and the 96 m crossing spire rebuilt after the fire of 15 April 2019.

Notre-Dame de Paris: the grand organ

systems.name: West towers
systems.description: The two 69 m west towers with their belfries, the 13 ton Emmanuel bourdon, and the 380 steps to the top.

systems.name: West facade
systems.description: The west front: three sculpted portals, the Gallery of Kings with its 28 statues, the 9.6 m rose window, and the Grand Gallery of chimeras.

systems.name: Nave
systems.description: The 12 m wide central vessel with its double aisles, rising 33 m to the rib vaults.

systems.name: Transept
systems.description: The shallow 48 m transept with its two great rose windows: 13.1 m to the north and 12.9 m to the south.

systems.name: Choir
systems.description: The 36 m choir with the high altar, the stalls, and the raised sanctuary.

systems.name: Chevet and apse
systems.description: The eastern chevet: outer wall, ambulatory, radiating chapels, and the half dome over the apse.

systems.name: Flying buttresses
systems.description: The flying buttresses added in the late 13th century to stop the walls bowing outward, among the earliest of their kind.

systems.name: Crossing spire
systems.description: The 96 m crossing spire: Viollet-le-Duc’s 1859 oak and lead flèche, destroyed in 2019 and rebuilt identically by 2024.

systems.name: Roofs
systems.description: The lead roofs and the Forest, the frame of more than 1,300 oak trees lost in the 2019 fire.

systems.name: Interior fittings
systems.description: Fittings of the interior: pulpit, pews, font, altars, treasury, and sacristy.

systems.name: Great organ
systems.description: The great organ: nearly 8,000 pipes, five keyboards, and 109 stops, 12 m tall above the west end of the nave.

systems.name: Parvis and setting
systems.description: The square in front of the cathedral with France’s Point Zero marker, the archaeological crypt, and the Charlemagne statue.
